1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5 Nbd7 5.N.strategy: Keeps the pin and the pressure on f6 rather than giving up the bishop for the knight. The bishop stays on the diagonal to d8, but Black's kingside pawns can be used to challenge it, so White's pin may not last.

Grabs the c4 pawn and gives up the centre for it, hoping to hold the pawn on the queenside. The line is tactical and risky: Black's kingside pawns are already committed and White gets space, development and open lines, so this suits only a player who knows the theory.
1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5 Nbd7 5.N.name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Knight Defence, Alekhine Gambit
